purpose_and_intended_use: For a temporary works engineer rebuilding permanent-works fundamentals, Eurocode fluency, and long-term capability for tightly scoped structural work. This is a multi-year syllabus, not a promise that you need to finish everything before becoming useful. Its purpose is to give you a complete map, with a realistic sequence and clear proof that you understand each stage.
professional_safeguard_notice: Educational learning curriculum and portfolio tracker only — not construction-ready design. All Eurocode, UK National Annex, and material checks require current controlled standards, verified project information, and independent professional checking before any real-world use.

multi_year_horizons.summary: Structural mechanics foundation + basic Eurocode workflow + a straightforward EC3 beam design.
Deeper steel, timber, masonry, residential alterations, basic geotechnics/foundations, and concrete fundamentals.
Integrated projects, analysis/model judgement, more complex stability, connections, professional practice, and building a portfolio of reviewed work.

year_one_outcome_statement: I can take a simple structural arrangement and identify the load path, support conditions, internal actions, deflected shape, tension/compression zones, likely failure modes, and stability requirements. I can establish basic ULS/SLS actions and work through a straightforward, laterally restrained Eurocode steel beam design while understanding the purpose and limitations of each check.

five_step_study_method.title: Explain it plainly
five_step_study_method.instruction: No equations at first. Explain what is physically happening.

five_step_study_method.title: Sketch it
five_step_study_method.instruction: Draw load paths, support conditions, deformed shape, compression/tension zones, and failure mode.

five_step_study_method.title: Calculate a simple case by hand
five_step_study_method.instruction: No software and no copied method.

five_step_study_method.title: Check it against a reliable source
five_step_study_method.instruction: A textbook worked answer, recognised professional guidance, or a checked/anonymised office example.

five_step_study_method.title: State assumptions and limits
five_step_study_method.instruction: What must be true for the calculation to be valid? What information is missing? What could change the answer?

calculation_note_structure.title: Brief and sketch
calculation_note_structure.prompt: Define the engineering problem, geometry, support idealisations, and an annotated structural sketch.

calculation_note_structure.title: Structural arrangement and load path
calculation_note_structure.prompt: Trace how vertical and lateral actions travel from point of application through members and supports to the ground.

calculation_note_structure.title: Design assumptions
calculation_note_structure.prompt: State idealisations, support fixity, restraint conditions, material models, and governing code/standard assumptions.

calculation_note_structure.title: Loads/actions
calculation_note_structure.prompt: List permanent, imposed, and other characteristic actions, tributary widths/areas, self-weight, and ULS/SLS combinations.

calculation_note_structure.title: Analysis
calculation_note_structure.prompt: Show equilibrium equations, support reactions, internal forces (N, V, M), SFDs, BMDs, and deflected shapes with explicit units.

calculation_note_structure.title: Checks
calculation_note_structure.prompt: Carry out section/member resistance, buckling/stability, bearing, and serviceability deflection checks.

calculation_note_structure.title: Detailing/restraint requirements
calculation_note_structure.prompt: Specify the physical details required to make the calculation assumptions true (bearing lengths, padstones, lateral/torsional restraint, connections).

calculation_note_structure.title: Conclusion
calculation_note_structure.prompt: State clearly what section/arrangement is proposed for learning purposes and which check governs.

calculation_note_structure.title: Limitations and questions requiring review
calculation_note_structure.prompt: Record missing site/ground information, exclusions, model limits, and specific questions for a senior or specialist engineer.

modules.short_title: Engineering maths, units and physical quantities

modules.title: Module 1 — Statics, equilibrium and load paths
modules.short_title: Statics, equilibrium and load paths
modules.why_it_matters: Free-body diagrams, support restraints, equilibrium reactions, tributary load takedown, and complete vertical and lateral load paths form the foundation of every structural calculation.
modules.verification_note: STAT-01 and STAT-02 have 6 interactive Phase 2 questions active (P2-FBD-01..03, P2-EQ-01..03). Examples 1.1–1.4 are mapped; tributary floor loading and falsework load-path exercises are scheduled for Milestone 2.
learn_topics: Free-body diagrams: isolate the structure/member; show all external loads; show reactions; choose axes; label dimensions and load positions
Equilibrium: ΣFx = 0; ΣFy = 0; ΣM = 0
Supports: roller support; pin support; fixed support; internal hinge; spring support, later; what each permits and restrains
Load paths: roof to walls/beams; floors to beams/walls; beams to columns/masonry; columns/walls to foundations; foundations to soil
Tributary areas: floor loading; roof loading; line loads to supports; load sharing assumptions
Stability: stable and unstable systems; determinate and indeterminate structures; why a stable load path is not enough if lateral restraint is missing

worked_examples.title: Beam reactions under UDL
worked_examples.description: A 6 m simply supported beam carries 10 kN/m. Calculate: total load; left reaction; right reaction; explain why symmetry applies.

worked_examples.title: Beam reactions under point load

worked_examples.title: Tributary floor load
worked_examples.description: A floor spans 4 m between two supporting beams. The beams are 5 m long. Floor actions are: permanent action: 1.0 kN/m²; imposed action: 1.5 kN/m². Calculate characteristic line loads to each beam, excluding beam self-weight.

worked_examples.description: Take a falsework arrangement you understand. Draw: wet concrete -> formwork -> primary beams -> secondary beams -> heads -> props/towers -> baseplates -> soleboards -> ground. Then list what could interrupt the load path.

modules.title: Module 2 — Internal actions, shear force and bending moment
modules.short_title: Internal actions, shear force and bending moment
modules.why_it_matters: Connects external loads and support reactions to internal axial force, shear force, bending moment, deflected shape, and tension/compression zones.
modules.verification_note: Objectives STAT-04 and BEAM-01..03 are mapped. Interactive SFD/BMD solver and Examples 2.1–2.3 practice questions are scheduled for Milestone 2.
learn_topics: Internal actions & diagrams: axial force; shear force; bending moment; sign conventions; cutting a member to reveal internal actions; SFDs; BMDs; load–shear–moment relationships; sagging/hogging; deflected shapes; tension and compression zones

Physical understanding: Axial tension pulls a member apart; Axial compression pushes it together and can lead to buckling; Shear tries to slide one part past another; Bending curves a member (one side in tension, the other in compression); Maximum bending often occurs where shear passes through zero; Maximum shear is often near supports, but actual loading arrangement matters

worked_examples.title: Simply supported UDL
worked_examples.description: Repeat the 6 m, 10 kN/m beam. Draw: SFD; BMD; deformed shape; tension/compression faces. Confirm: Vmax = wL/2 and Mmax = wL²/8.

worked_examples.title: Cantilever under UDL

worked_examples.title: Point load beam
worked_examples.description: Use the 5 m beam with the 20 kN point load. Draw SFD/BMD and find the maximum moment from the diagram.

modules.title: Module 3 — Stress, strain, stiffness and material behaviour
modules.short_title: Stress, strain, stiffness and material behaviour
modules.why_it_matters: Distinguishes internal force from stress, deformation from strain, and material stiffness (E, G) from material strength across steel, concrete, timber, and masonry.
modules.verification_note: Semantic quantities for Stress, Young's Modulus E, and Shear Modulus G are implemented in domain/quantities.py. Interactive exercises for Examples 3.1–3.3 are scheduled for Milestone 2.
learn_topics: Stress and strain: normal stress σ = F/A; strain ε = ΔL/L; stress–strain curves; elastic range; yield; plastic deformation; ultimate strength; fracture
Stiffness: axial deformation ΔL = PL/AE; Young’s modulus E; shear modulus G; Poisson’s ratio ν; relationship for isotropic materials E = 2G(1+ν)
Materials: structural steel; reinforced concrete; timber; masonry; ductile versus brittle behaviour; creep, shrinkage, fatigue: introductory awareness

worked_examples.title: Steel tie
worked_examples.description: A steel tie: length: 3,000 mm; area: 1,000 mm²; tension force: 100 kN; E = 200,000 N/mm². Calculate: stress; strain; extension.

worked_examples.title: Steel versus aluminium stiffness
worked_examples.description: Two bars have the same area, length, and applied force. One is steel and one is aluminium. Calculate/compare extensions using representative Young’s moduli.

worked_examples.title: Material comparison note

modules.title: Module 4 — Section properties, bending theory and member shape
modules.short_title: Section properties, bending theory and member shape
modules.why_it_matters: This is one of your most important modules. Explains how cross-sectional geometry (A, I, Z, W_pl, i) governs bending stress, flexural stiffness, plastic hinge formation, and why major vs minor axis orientation is critical.
modules.verification_note: Deterministic elastic bending stress (σ = M/W_el and σ = My/I) and semantic quantity guards (Q vs W_el vs W_pl, I vs J vs I_t) are active. Interactive questions for Examples 4.1–4.4 are scheduled for Milestone 2.
learn_topics: Geometry and centroids: area; centroid; neutral axis; symmetrical and unsymmetrical shapes; composite areas
Second moment of area: I; major/minor axes; parallel-axis theorem; why I depends on axis; units of I: mm⁴
Section modulus: elastic section modulus Z = I/y; elastic bending stress σ = My/I = M/Z; plastic section modulus; elastic versus plastic stress distributions; plastic hinge concept
Radius of gyration: i = √(I/A) and its relevance to buckling later

Why I-sections work: bending stresses are greatest furthest from the neutral axis; flanges resist most bending; web keeps flanges apart and carries shear; material near neutral axis contributes less to bending resistance; depth generally improves bending stiffness/resistance strongly
Major and minor axes: for a typical universal beam, major axis = strong bending axis, minor axis = weak bending axis; orientation and restraint matter

worked_examples.title: Rectangle section properties
worked_examples.description: For a 75 mm × 225 mm rectangular timber section: I = bd³/12. Calculate I, Z, and bending stress for M = 8 kNm. Repeat with depth increased to 300 mm. Write what changed: bending stress, stiffness, likely deflection, practical limitations.

worked_examples.title: Parallel-axis theorem
worked_examples.description: Calculate the second moment of area of a simple built-up section made from two rectangular flanges and a web.

worked_examples.title: Major/minor axis of a UB
worked_examples.description: Use a section table from SCI/SteelConstruction.info. Choose one UB and identify: major-axis I; minor-axis I; major/minor elastic section modulus; ratio between them; why using the section in the wrong orientation is dangerous.

worked_examples.title: Elastic versus plastic bending
worked_examples.description: Sketch a rectangular steel section under increasing bending: (1) elastic stress distribution; (2) first yield at extreme fibres; (3) fully plastic stress block. Then write why local buckling or LTB may prevent full plastic resistance being used.

SteelConstruction.info: steel section properties and section classification introductions.

modules.short_title: Deflection, serviceability and vibration
modules.why_it_matters: A beam can be safe against collapse (ULS) but still unacceptable in service (SLS) because it cracks finishes, binds doors/windows, damages partitions, ponds water, feels bouncy, or looks visibly sagged.

worked_examples.description: For a simply supported beam: δmax = 5wL⁴/(384EI). Explain why increased steel grade does not materially alter elastic deflection.

modules.title: Module 6 — Failure modes, buckling, restraint and stability
modules.short_title: Failure modes, buckling, restraint and stability
modules.why_it_matters: Slender compression struts, unrestrained beams, and partially erected frames frequently fail by stability loss (flexural buckling, LTB, sway, overturning) well before reaching material squash or yield strength.
modules.verification_note: Curriculum structure and Examples 6.1–6.4 are seeded. Interactive Euler buckling and stability checks are scheduled for Milestone 2.
learn_topics: Material-related failure: yielding; tensile rupture; compression crushing; shear failure; bearing failure; fatigue; brittle fracture: awareness
Stability-related failure: local buckling; flexural buckling; torsional buckling; flexural-torsional buckling; lateral torsional buckling; plate buckling; global frame sway; overturning; sliding
Buckling fundamentals: Euler buckling; effective length; end restraints; slenderness; imperfection sensitivity; why increasing area alone may not efficiently solve a buckling problem

LTB: compression flange moves laterally; member twists; beam loses bending capacity before reaching full section resistance; restraint must restrain the relevant flange and/or torsional rotation; construction sequence may change restraint
Building stability: braced frames; moment frames; shear walls; diaphragms; ties; load paths under wind/lateral loads

worked_examples.title: Euler column comparison
worked_examples.description: Compare pinned-pinned and fixed-fixed columns of equal section and length. Use: Pcr = π²EI/Lcr². Explain what changes when effective length reduces.

worked_examples.title: LTB sketch
worked_examples.description: Take a long steel beam under gravity load. Draw: tension flange; compression flange; sideways compression-flange movement; twisting; possible restraint points from slab/deck/purlins; torsional restraint at supports.

worked_examples.title: Frame stability
worked_examples.description: Draw a simple single-storey frame: (1) no bracing; (2) diagonal bracing; (3) moment frame. Apply a horizontal load and explain what prevents sway in each case.

worked_examples.title: Temporary versus permanent stability
worked_examples.description: Identify a temporary condition where a completed structure is stable but an intermediate stage is not (e.g. steel frame before permanent bracing/floor diaphragm; masonry wall before floor/roof restraint; slab during wet concrete loading; precast elements before permanent tying).

modules.title: Module 7 — Basis of design, actions and Eurocode philosophy
modules.short_title: Basis of design, actions and Eurocode philosophy
modules.why_it_matters: Connects first-principles mechanics to the Eurocode reliability framework (EN 1990 / EN 1991 + UK National Annexes), distinguishing characteristic actions from factored ULS/SLS design action effects.
modules.verification_note: Requires user verification against current controlled copies of EN 1990, EN 1991, and UK National Annexes. Do not rely on unverified partial factors.
learn_topics: Design philosophy: characteristic value; design value; action effect; resistance; partial factors; limit states; design situations; reliability; National Annexes; assumptions and model uncertainty
Actions: permanent actions; imposed actions; snow; wind; construction loads; accidental actions; thermal effects: awareness; earth/water pressures: awareness
Limit states: ULS; SLS; rare/frequent/quasi-permanent combinations where relevant; combinations and accompanying actions

Calculation workflow: (1) define structural system; (2) establish actions; (3) identify combinations; (4) calculate design action effects; (5) determine design resistance; (6) compare; (7) check serviceability; (8) provide detailing/restraint requirements; (9) document assumptions and limitations

learn_topics: Masonry behaviour & checks: masonry units, mortar, wall types; compression-dominated behaviour; low tensile capacity; concentrated loads; bearing and padstones; lateral restraint; slenderness; openings and lintels; cavity walls; movement joints; cracking
Alterations & temporary works: existing structure uncertainty; surveys; hidden conditions; temporary support/propping; foundation implications

worked_examples.title: New opening in load-bearing masonry
worked_examples.description: Use a textbook/recognised worked example or anonymised office calculation. Assess: existing wall arrangement; loading onto wall; beam loading; bearing lengths; padstone need; wall compression/bearing considerations; effects on lower storey walls/foundations; lateral restraint; temporary propping concept; construction sequencing; unknown-information risk.

resources: IStructE guidance, where available.
Masonry industry technical guidance.
EC6 and National Annex through work/library.
Search: masonry padstone bearing structural design UK; existing masonry opening structural assessment; masonry wall lateral restraint guidance.
gate_requirements: explain why 'sizing the steel beam' alone is not a complete alteration design
account for all 10 system elements: beam, bearings, wall capacity, padstone, support below, foundations, lateral restraint, temporary works, survey uncertainty, and construction sequence

modules.title: Module 12 — Soil mechanics and geotechnical fundamentals
modules.short_title: Soil mechanics and geotechnical fundamentals
modules.why_it_matters: Every permanent structure and temporary prop/tower ultimately transfers load into the ground; understanding effective stress, groundwater, drained vs undrained shear strength, settlement, and GI reports is essential.
modules.verification_note: Years 2–3 module (linked to Integrated Milestone E). Curriculum metadata and Examples 12.1–12.3 are seeded; interactive soil mechanics checks are awaiting Milestone 2+ development.
learn_topics: Soil types and description: gravel; sand; silt; clay; organic soils; made ground; grading; plasticity; density; water content
Stress in soil: total stress; pore-water pressure; effective stress σ′ = σ − u; why effective stress controls many soil strength/deformation behaviours
Water and drainage: permeability; groundwater; seepage; drained versus undrained behaviour; short-term versus long-term conditions
Shear strength: friction; cohesion; Mohr-Coulomb relationship τ = c′ + σ′ tan φ′; what each term represents physically; limitations of the model
Settlement: immediate settlement; consolidation; differential settlement; why settlement often governs even where bearing resistance is adequate

Ground investigation: desk study; walkover; boreholes; trial pits; CPT/SPT: awareness; factual versus interpretative reports; ground model; uncertainty; contamination, utilities, trees, drainage, adjacent structures

worked_examples.title: Effective stress
worked_examples.description: At a given depth, calculate: total vertical stress; pore-water pressure; effective vertical stress; for a soil profile with groundwater at a stated level.

worked_examples.title: Shear strength concept
worked_examples.description: Use supplied c′, φ′, and effective normal stress values to calculate shear strength from the Mohr-Coulomb equation. Then explain why the input parameters cannot be guessed for real design.

worked_examples.title: Ground investigation reading exercise
worked_examples.description: Find a factual ground investigation report through a public authority/university search. Identify: site location and history; borehole/trial pit locations; strata; groundwater observations; testing; made ground; limitations; whether it provides design parameters or only factual information.

resources: Craig’s Soil Mechanics.
Das, Principles of Geotechnical Engineering.
ICE and CIRIA resources.
Search: "factual ground investigation report" pdf; "geotechnical interpretive report" pdf; effective stress worked example soil mechanics; site:gov.uk ground investigation report PDF.
gate_requirements: explain effective stress in plain English
explain why groundwater matters
distinguish drained/undrained conditions at a basic level
distinguish bearing failure from settlement
read a basic GI report critically
state when a geotechnical engineer must be involved

modules.title: Module 13 — Foundations and retaining structures
modules.short_title: Foundations and retaining structures
modules.why_it_matters: Links geotechnical behaviour with structural design of strip/pad/raft foundations and retaining structures (bearing, eccentricity, settlement, sliding, overturning, bending, one-way and punching shear).
modules.verification_note: Years 2–3 module (linked to Integrated Milestones E and F). Requires EC7/EC2 + UK National Annexes and Concrete Centre / Craig / Das references.
learn_topics: Foundations: strip foundations; pad foundations; raft foundations; piles: introductory awareness; ground beams; underpinning: awareness; existing foundations and uncertainty

Foundation checks: bearing resistance; settlement; eccentricity; contact pressure; sliding; overturning; structural bending; one-way shear; punching shear; reinforcement detailing; drainage and adjacent excavations

Retaining structures: lateral earth pressures; active/passive/at-rest concepts; drainage; sliding; overturning; bearing; global stability; surcharge; water pressure; buried services/adjacent structures

worked_examples.title: RC pad foundation
worked_examples.description: Using credible supplied ground parameters from a textbook or checked training example: establish column load and moment; choose trial pad dimensions; calculate bearing pressure; assess eccentricity; consider bearing and settlement limitations; check pad bending; check one-way shear; check punching shear; prepare reinforcement sketch; identify what geotechnical information would be required in real life.

resources: Concrete Centre for RC foundation/punching material.
EC7/EC2 resources via employer/library.
Craig/Das for underlying soil concepts.
Search: pad foundation design Eurocode worked example; reinforced concrete pad foundation punching shear worked example; foundation eccentricity bearing pressure example.
gate_requirements: explain why average pressure is not enough
explain why a safe foundation must address soil and structural checks
explain why settlement may govern
explain why foundation design relies on credible ground information
explain why retaining walls require drainage and global stability consideration

modules.title: Module 14 — Reinforced concrete design to EC2
modules.short_title: Reinforced concrete design to EC2
modules.why_it_matters: Builds fundamental understanding of cracked reinforced concrete section behaviour, strain compatibility, ductile under-reinforced flexure, shear links, punching shear, anchorage/curtailment detailing, and striking/backpropping.
modules.verification_note: Years 2–3 module. Requires EN 1992-1-1 + UK NA, Mosley/Bungey/Hulse, and Concrete Centre guides.
learn_topics: RC behaviour: concrete compression; concrete tension/cracking; steel reinforcement; strain compatibility; neutral axis; lever arm; under-reinforced versus over-reinforced behaviour; ductility
RC beams: flexural design; singly reinforced sections; doubly reinforced sections: awareness; shear; links/stirrups; anchorage; laps; curtailment; cover; deflection; cracking
Slabs and columns: one-way slabs; two-way action: introduction; punching shear; columns and slenderness: introduction
Durability and construction: exposure classes; fire; cover; compaction; curing; propping and striking; early-age loading; construction joints

worked_examples.title: RC beam
worked_examples.description: Design a simply supported RC beam: actions and combinations; preliminary sizing; bending reinforcement; shear reinforcement; serviceability; cover/exposure; anchorage; detailing sketch.

worked_examples.title: RC slab strip
worked_examples.description: Design a one-way slab strip: tributary width; moment; reinforcement; shear; deflection/cracking awareness; support detailing.

worked_examples.title: Punching shear awareness
worked_examples.description: Use a flat slab/column example from a recognised text to understand: critical perimeter; why punching occurs; why local thickening or reinforcement may be needed.

resources: Mosley, Bungey and Hulse — Reinforced Concrete Design to Eurocode 2.
The Concrete Centre.
EC2 and National Annex.
Search: Concrete Centre EC2 beam worked example; reinforced concrete beam shear links worked example; EC2 punching shear worked example.
gate_requirements: explain why bottom reinforcement is used at midspan in a simply supported beam
explain why top reinforcement may be needed over supports
explain why links are required
explain why detailing and anchorage are design-critical
explain why concrete cannot be treated as just 'steel design with different factors'

modules.title: Module 15 — Structural analysis beyond simple beams
modules.short_title: Structural analysis beyond simple beams
modules.why_it_matters: Extends analysis to trusses, plane/portal frames, continuous beams, and statically indeterminate structures where relative stiffness and compatibility govern force distribution.
modules.verification_note: Years 3–4+ module. Mapped to SYS-01 and SYS-02; interactive truss/frame problems are scheduled for later milestones.
learn_topics: Systems & indeterminacy: trusses; plane frames; portal frames; arches: introductory; continuous beams; moment distribution: awareness; stiffness method concept; determinate versus indeterminate structures; compatibility; redistribution: awareness; influence lines: introductory; second-order effects; imperfections; dynamic effects: introductory

worked_examples.title: Continuous two-span beam
worked_examples.description: Analyse a continuous two-span beam and compare hogging support moments and sagging span moments against simply supported spans.

worked_examples.title: Simple truss reactions/member forces
worked_examples.description: Calculate global support reactions and internal axial tension/compression member forces in a determinate pin-jointed truss.

worked_examples.title: Simple portal frame under vertical and lateral load
worked_examples.description: Trace reactions, deflected shape, and bending moment distribution in a simple portal frame under gravity and lateral actions.

worked_examples.title: Compare determinate hand result with software result
worked_examples.description: Compare a hand-calculated determinate structure against structural analysis software output.

resources: Hibbeler Structural Analysis.
Jeff Hanson, where relevant.
Employer software training and checked examples.
gate_requirements: identify whether an analysis is determinate
understand why indeterminate structures redistribute force according to stiffness
explain why connection stiffness/restraint changes force distribution
perform basic hand validation of a simple model

modules.title: Module 16 — Software modelling and model validation
modules.short_title: Software modelling and model validation
modules.why_it_matters: Prevents 'garbage-in, garbage-out' software reliance by training rigorous inspection of releases, restraints, local axes, load combinations, reaction equilibrium, and deformed shapes.
modules.verification_note: Years 3–4+ module. Seeded with worked project templates and the 7 mandatory model-interrogation gate questions.
learn_topics: Modelling & validation: idealisation; member local axes; releases; supports; springs; load cases; combinations; offsets; eccentricities; diaphragm assumptions; bracing; 2D/3D models; meshing: awareness; second-order analysis; model warnings; reactions checks; sensitivity checks; hand checks

worked_examples.title: Beam hand check versus software
worked_examples.description: Model a simple beam in your available software. Then: calculate reactions/moment/shear manually; compare results; deliberately change a release; deliberately remove a restraint; inspect the changed behaviour; write why the model changed.

worked_examples.title: Braced frame model
worked_examples.description: Model a simple braced frame: verify vertical reactions; apply lateral load; identify bracing force; check deflected shape; compare with expected physical behaviour.

resources: Employer structural analysis software documentation and checked verification examples.
IStructE / NAFEMS guidance on validation of structural analysis models.
gate_requirements: ask every time: What is the load path?
ask every time: What stops translation?
ask every time: What stops rotation?
ask every time: Does the model’s restraint exist in real life?
ask every time: Do reactions balance applied load?
ask every time: Is the deformed shape plausible?
ask every time: What could the model be missing?

modules.title: Module 17 — Design detailing, drawings and construction interface
modules.short_title: Design detailing, drawings and construction interface
modules.why_it_matters: A calculation is only valid if the drawings and construction details physically realise the assumed restraints, bearings, connections, and erection sequence on site.
modules.verification_note: Years 3–4+ module. Seeded with practical drawing-audit exercises and calculation-to-detail verification checklists.
learn_topics: Drawings & site interface: drawing reading; member schedules; GA drawings; connection details; reinforcement drawings; timber details; tolerances; bearings; movement joints; temporary stability; erection sequence; interfaces with architecture/MEP; RFIs and technical queries; design changes; inspection and hold points

worked_examples.title: Anonymised work drawing and detail audit
worked_examples.description: Take anonymised drawings from work, where permitted, and ask: what is the structural system? what is the load path? what assumptions are embedded in this detail? how is lateral restraint provided? how is the design built? what could be misinterpreted on site?

resources: Anonymised project GA and detail drawings (where permitted).
SCI, Concrete Centre, TRADA, and IStructE standard detailing guides.
gate_requirements: identify where a calculation requires a drawing/detail to make it true (e.g. a beam 'restrained by floor' needs a real restraint detail; a pinned connection needs rotation capacity; a foundation calculation needs excavation/bearing/reinforcement/concrete details; a timber check needs clear assumptions for notches, holes, connections, and moisture exposure)

modules.title: Module 18 — Existing structures, surveys and uncertainty
modules.short_title: Existing structures, surveys and uncertainty
modules.why_it_matters: Existing buildings rarely match record drawings; safe alteration engineering depends on systematic surveys, material/defect recognition, temporary stability planning, and knowing when not to guess.
modules.verification_note: Years 3–4+ module. Seeded with historic alteration survey and uncertainty exercise.
learn_topics: Appraisal & uncertainty: existing drawings versus reality; visual surveys; intrusive investigation; material identification; deterioration; corrosion; timber rot; masonry cracking; movement; hidden supports; unknown foundations; temporary stability during alterations; conservative assumptions; when not to assume; monitoring and specialist survey

worked_examples.title: Historic alteration survey and uncertainty assessment
worked_examples.description: Take an anonymised historic alteration project or published case study. Prepare: information required before design; survey checklist; uncertainties; potential load path; likely risks; temporary works considerations; when to involve geotechnical/specialist input.

resources: IStructE Appraisal of Existing Structures guidance, where available.
BRE / CIRIA building defect and structural appraisal publications.
gate_requirements: state clearly: 'I cannot safely finalise this design until I know X, Y, and Z' — recognising that refusing to guess unknown conditions is good engineering judgement, not a weakness

modules.title: Module 19 — Professional practice, checking and business readiness
modules.short_title: Professional practice, checking and business readiness
modules.why_it_matters: Defines the professional boundaries of safe engineering practice: clear scope, explicit exclusions, required pre-design information, independent checking levels, competence boundaries, and escalation.
modules.verification_note: Years 3–4+ ongoing module. Seeded with the 7-part Project Scope, Checking, and Escalation Governance template.
learn_topics: Professional governance: scope definition; fee proposals; exclusions; appointments/contracts; professional indemnity awareness; design responsibility; checking levels; calculation checking; drawing checking; design risk management; document control; CPD; competence assessment; client communication; contractor communication; quality management; limitations and reliance on specialist information

worked_examples.title: 7-Part Project Scope, Checking and Escalation Statement
worked_examples.description: For any project, write: (1) Scope — what you are designing; (2) Exclusions — what you are not designing; (3) Information required — what must be provided before design; (4) Assumptions — what you have assumed; (5) Constraints — what site/construction conditions must be met; (6) Checking — who reviews the work and at what level; (7) Escalation — when specialist or senior review is required.

resources: IStructE / ICE Code of Conduct and professional practice guidelines.
BS 5975 procedural control and design checking categories (Cat 0, 1, 2, 3).
gate_requirements: define a safe scope
recognise work beyond your competence
communicate uncertainty
arrange checking
avoid accepting unbounded liability for unknown conditions

portfolio_milestones.title: Milestone A — Structural mechanics portfolio
portfolio_milestones.description: Complete and file: 10 equilibrium/reaction problems; 10 SFD/BMD problems; 5 bending-stress/section-property problems; 5 deflection problems; 5 buckling/stability sketches.
portfolio_milestones.pass_condition: You can explain each one without notes.

portfolio_milestones.title: Milestone B — First EC3 beam package
portfolio_milestones.description: Produce a complete learning calculation package for a laterally restrained beam.

required_items.label: Complete 17-item learning calculation package for a laterally restrained EC3 steel beam

portfolio_milestones.pass_condition: A senior engineer can read it and see: coherent assumptions; correct workflow; sensible loading; credible restraint; understandable conclusion.

portfolio_milestones.title: Milestone C — Construction-stage case study
portfolio_milestones.description: Choose a real or historic temporary works situation. Prepare: permanent condition; temporary condition; load path; stability system; sequencing risk; controls/checks.

required_items.label: Construction-stage temporary vs permanent condition case study

portfolio_milestones.pass_condition: You can articulate why the temporary condition may govern even where the permanent structure is safe.

portfolio_milestones.title: Milestone D — Timber/masonry alteration study
portfolio_milestones.description: Produce a learning case for a straightforward opening or timber floor beam.

required_items.label: Full-system timber floor beam or load-bearing masonry opening learning case

portfolio_milestones.pass_condition: You identify the whole system, not just the new beam.

portfolio_milestones.title: Milestone E — Foundation and ground report review
portfolio_milestones.description: Read one factual ground investigation report and prepare: ground profile; groundwater observations; limitations; implications for foundation design; questions requiring a geotechnical engineer.

required_items.label: Factual ground investigation report critical review and foundation implications note

portfolio_milestones.pass_condition: Demonstrates critical reading of factual ground data, groundwater effects, limitations, and clear geotechnical escalation triggers.

portfolio_milestones.title: Milestone F — Integrated small-building scheme
portfolio_milestones.description: Complete a hypothetical small extension/alteration package: load path from roof/floor to ground; actions and combinations; steel/timber/masonry elements; foundation concept; temporary support concept; design risk register; assumptions and limitations; list of independent checks/specialist input. This is a learning portfolio, not construction-ready work.

required_items.label: Hypothetical small extension/alteration multi-element learning portfolio package

portfolio_milestones.pass_condition: Complete integrated learning portfolio demonstrating roof-to-ground load path, element checks, temporary works concept, risk register, and independent checking schedule.
